evidence.positive: On the fresh boot of 6810750a1, databasechangelog in all four tenant schemas (demo-demo, mgb-mgh, mgb-icsnh, mayo-mayo) holds 242-drop-operations-classification as EXECUTED (orderexecuted 400, right after 228-backfill-straggler-acuity at 388) and information_schema.columns lists only acuity, no classification, on every operations table. The app still reads and writes Operation rows without the column: POST /api/app-launch for demo-demo patient-1 / case-2823 as loopuser returned 200 and created the operations row (case_id=case-2823, acuity set later via SQL), and GET /api/admin/patients/by-pmrn/patient-1/operations as admin returned 200 with the operation. Strongest runtime proof came from the revert: after re-adding demo-demo.operations.classification with a row where classification = acuity ('Elective') and deleting the 242 changelog row, restarting the app re-ran the change-set, databasechangelog shows 242 EXECUTED at 15:31:45, the column was gone, and the app reached /actuator/health/readiness UP with 'Started OrciApplication in 11.849 seconds' and no guard message in the log.
evidence.negative: Re-run is a no-op: with the column already dropped, deleting demo-demo's 242 changelog row and restarting the app produced 242 EXECUTED again (15:32:13) with zero 'Refusing to drop' or 'encountered an exception' lines in the post-restart log, readiness UP in ~15s, and the admin operations read plus a second app-launch of the same case both returned 200 afterwards. Also, during both red checks the drop did not happen and nothing was cascaded: after each halt information_schema still showed operations.classification and the test view v_or2823_classification intact, so a halted guard loses nothing (no CASCADE path).
evidence.red_check: Flip A (data disagree): ALTER TABLE "demo-demo".operations ADD COLUMN classification, set the row to acuity='Elective', classification='Urgent', deleted the 242 databasechangelog row, docker restart. Liquibase logged 'ChangeSet ...242-drop-operations-classification::theo encountered an exception' followed by the onFailMessage 'Refusing to drop operations.classification. Rows with a null acuity: ...', the liquibaseTenant bean failed, and the container exited with code 1. Flip B (dependent view): set classification = acuity, CREATE VIEW v_or2823_classification AS SELECT case_id, classification FROM operations, started the container again: same 'Refusing to drop operations.classification' halt, container exited 1, column and view both still present. Reverted by DROP VIEW and restarting: 242 EXECUTED, column dropped, app UP; the guard string appears zero times in the post-revert logs.

red_check_signature: Refusing to drop operations.classification. Rows with a null acuity
caveats: The flip-and-revert ran against one tenant schema (demo-demo); the other three were only observed in their post-boot dropped state.
The ticket's deploy prerequisite that no R1 pod is still alive at rollout time is operational and not checkable here; the guard does not detect live pods, only data and view dependencies.

Production operations rows and analytics views were not inspected; the guard is what enforces the reconciliation and view prerequisites at deploy time, and this run only proves the guard halts and never cascades.
lock_timeout = 5s was not exercised under concurrent load; no reader held a lock on operations during the drop here.
No pre-fix class swap: the change is a Liquibase change-set with no Java diff, so the red check used data flips only.

automation.assessment: No test exercises change-set 242. The existing Liquibase tests (LiquidbaseConfigurationTest, ChangelogTemporalTypeTest) lint changelog files rather than run them, and BaseDataJpaTest builds the schema from entities so it never runs migrations. This is a one-way, one-shot contract step that has already been applied everywhere it runs, so a runtime migration test earns little after deploy; the durable value is a cheap lint that keeps the retired column from creeping back into changelogs or analytics SQL.
proposed_tests: Changelog lint (alongside ChangelogTemporalTypeTest): no change-set numbered above 242 and no file under orci/src/main/analytics references operations.classification, so the dropped column cannot be reintroduced by a later migration or view.

Integration-tests profile only: apply the tenant changelog to a Testcontainers schema seeded with the pre-R3 operations shape and a disagreeing acuity/classification row, assert MigrationFailedException whose message contains 'Refusing to drop operations.classification' and that the column still exists afterwards; repeat with a dependent view; then settle the row, drop the view, re-run, and assert the column is gone and a second run is a no-op.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: On a fresh boot the drop change-set is EXECUTED in all four tenant schemas, operations has acuity and no classification, and case start plus operation reads work against the dropped schema; re-adding the column with consistent data and re-running the change-set dropped it again and the app booted.
Negative: Re-running the change-set on an already-dropped schema executes as a no-op with no guard message, and a halted guard leaves the column and its dependent view untouched.
Red check: Re-adding the column with a row where classification disagreed with acuity, and separately with a view reading the column, made the guard halt the boot with the refusing-to-drop message, and both were reverted.

Automation: A changelog lint keeping operations.classification out of later change-sets and analytics SQL is worth adding; a Testcontainers migration test for the guard is optional.
